title: The Leading Ones
subtitle: In days like this, nothing is more important than security.

trails.title: Letters from Readers
trails.description: The smudged part of an copy of abandoned newspaper.

content.text:
"HEART OF THE OCEAN"
COLLECTION OF SUSPICIOUS INFORMATION

{p}At that time I was groping for my glasses on the floor. When I look up, I saw it. The ominous, fleeting shadow. I also found an evidence of its appearance on the floor: a dark animal hair, different to humans'. Undoubtedly, our thief is a black animal, or some kind of a flying dragon. I've read about them from the books, they like shiny objects, like jewels or nicely decorated glasses.
                        —A friendly tourist who has high myopia
{p}According to my theory, the
thief is an adult male who
has very poor manners. He
has a bewildered black beard
which falls out easily. He has
strong hands though, strong
enough to knock over a robot.
                         —An awkward detective trying a bit too hard to convince his listeners

As it turns out, the security robots are far from reliable. These tin heads can never replace us. They are clumsy, and use up a lot of oil, which is hardly environmentally friendly, isn't it? The big men in the parliament should really look into this company and see if there is anything fishy. That's why we poor securities voted for them ...
                          —An aggrieved security guard (former){img}

items.speaker: Newsboy
items.text: Breaking news! Breaking news today!

items.speaker: Newsboy
items.text: The New Humans Company announced they'd offer another reward for the 13th International Jewelry Show. The company claimed that the person who filches The Heart of London can collect a £1 million reward at No. 15 Bond Street.

items.speaker: Newsboy
items.text: Reliable news sources reveal that several people have failed and been arrested, including big names like Greedy Jack, crime duo Pain and Drizzt ... Oh, excuse me! Hello!

items.speaker: Newsboy
items.text: Excuse me, the beautiful lady in black. Are you interested in the news of today? Grab a copy!
Are you talking to me?

items.speaker: Newsboy
items.text: Yeah, you've turned around, that's to say ...

items.speaker: Newsboy
items.text: Ah ... your ...

items.speaker: Newsboy
items.text: Sorry. My ... my bad. I didn't notice your ... uniqueness ...
No need to apologize, warm-hearted child. Could you please read me the news of the day?
I will pay appropriately.

items.speaker: Newsboy
items.text: Sure, my generous lady! Please, sit right here to get away from the crowds.

items.speaker: Newsboy
items.text: *coughs* Hope you don't mind my raspy voice.

items.speaker: Newsboy
items.text: "London faces severe public security issues. Approval rating might drop."

items.speaker: Newsboy
items.text: "Ace Café prepares for Motorcycle Road Racing, government failed to halt."

items.speaker: Newsboy
items.text: "Rock pirate hijacks radio frequency, claiming 'fun is about to begin.'"

items.speaker: Newsboy
items.text: "Artistic freak on street. Police warning over colorful bubbles." ...
Yes. Today is the day when multiple breaking news is published in the newspaper.
A wave of street culture, the conflict between the new and old order, and a young artist desiring to step onto the stage under the spotlight …
Heh heh ...
That will be a fantastic plot to start the story.
City of London Police
In a corner of the room, an unexpected "guest" sneaks in through the window. He closes the sergeant's drawer without making any noise.
Everyone in the office has their own business and thus pays no attention to such a slight action.

items.speaker: Iverson
items.text: We are here with full sincerity, Sergeant William.

items.speaker: Sergeant
items.text: Certainly. You made all our headlines. Londoners know what you've done.

items.speaker: Sergeant
items.text: However, your proposal for security companies in maintaining the security of London doesn't conform to the principles of law enforcement.

items.speaker: Sergeant
items.text: What's more, the public is still alert to security companies.

items.speaker: Sergeant
items.text: You know, after the Ramirez Incident, people no longer trust security companies ...

items.speaker: Iverson
items.text: Ramirez? Oh, Jesus! Why do you compare us with an "arcanist company"?

items.speaker: Iverson
items.text: They never make any security plans, nor do they resort to weapons or force. The only thing they have is the stupid brainwave, which definitely brings all kinds of trouble.

items.speaker: Iverson
items.text: They even claim possessing "the imagination that goes beyond all thieves." Good heavens, do you believe that? Why would a security company think as a thief?

items.speaker: Sergeant
items.text: Well, hard to believe, though, they did create many miracles, just like what you are doing.

items.speaker: Iverson
items.text: Humph! Security that lives on the irrealistic "imagination" can amaze the public shortly, but the efficacy never lasts long.

items.speaker: Iverson
items.text: We are not that desperate to deceive the public with a fake trophy, nor will we commit suicide in the fear of punishment like their founder.

items.speaker: Iverson
items.text: Sergeant William, please trust us that New Humans is a robotics company doing the right cause. We have a well-formulated Guidance on Security.
Iverson presses the button with a pleased look.
A strange robot steps into the room.

items.speaker: Iverson
items.text: This is our latest product—Security Control Type I.

items.speaker: Iverson
items.text: It carries abundant security measures, including tear gas, endive worm powder, magnetic interference unit, and can detect any threat within a radius of five meters.

items.speaker: Iverson
items.text: Most importantly, it is fully under control and reacts to emergencies with 173 inbuilt programmes. Ha! I think it is a reliable helping hand of our police officers.

items.speaker: Iverson
items.text: Just like now, if we switch on its sensor ...
Suddenly, the robot makes a loud warning sound.

items.speaker: Security Robot
items.text: Suspicious invader detected. Location: right under the first office desk, the second ... the third ... The target is moving quickly.

items.speaker: Sergeant
items.text: Is it going wrong?

items.speaker: Iverson
items.text: It never goes wrong.
Iverson quickly walks to the curtain.
The curtain is opened. A sneaking figure stands up.
Hey! Hey!
Gentlemen, and this very sensitive robot friend, hello!

items.speaker: Sergeant
items.text: You! Again? Where's ... Thomson, get in here and kick him out right now!

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: Wait, wait! I just want to talk to you about the watering car. Look ...

items.speaker: Sergeant
items.text: I've told you a hundred times. Nobody ever cares about those God-knows-what pop elements.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: Pop, yes, pop! You just spoke it out. Currently, pop is still too avant-garde, so I'm very glad to meet someone with the same taste!

items.speaker: Sergeant
items.text: That's because you've tediously repeated it for ages!

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: So you can understand our philosophy, and I believe others will ...

items.speaker: Iverson
items.text: I get it. This is a malicious rulebreaker. Such kind of violation can be tackled by the security plan installed in our robot.

items.speaker: Iverson
items.text: Sergeant William, here is another reason why London needs our robot.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: Robot ...?

items.speaker: Iverson
items.text: It's the new measure prepared for all discontented rulebreakers like you.

items.speaker: Iverson
items.text: It will stop all your willful actions. Any violations will be severely restricted by our security robot!
Diggers pats the head of the robot.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: It looks not reliable at all.
Diggers pokes the body of the robot.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: And it's not as soft as police dogs, either.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: You should try shaking hands with those fluffy shepherds. It helps shape the emotional system of your robot.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: Puppies are friendly, lovely, and they can read your mind.

items.speaker: Iverson
items.text: Ugh! Such a lame idea.

items.speaker: Iverson
items.text: Some people don't like those plushy quadrupeds. It's so difficult to get their hair off our noses and clothes. And their smell stinks.

items.speaker: Iverson
items.text: Sergeant, now I will present you Security Control Type I—Moralization.

items.speaker: Iverson
items.text: It has an all-round precaution plan installed for all citizens. And of course, it knows how to cope with you hooligans.

items.speaker: Iverson
items.text: It doesn't rely on some impalpable "imagination."

items.speaker: Sergeant
items.text: Totally controllable?

items.speaker: Iverson
items.text: For sure.
Iverson presses another button.
The robot starts to blink in red and walks towards Diggers.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: Hey! Malfunctioning, you iron monster?

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: Keep away from me! What's in your hand? Pu-put it down. That's rude!

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: We want peace, not war!
Iverson presses the switch with pleasure.
The robot calms down.

items.speaker: Iverson
items.text: As you've seen, Sergeant William, our robot excelled.

items.speaker: Iverson
items.text: According to our research data, New Humans is winning the public. People trust robots.

items.speaker: Iverson
items.text: They are looking forward to a safer and more peaceful London.

items.speaker: Sergeant
items.text: Wow! The talent Mr. Robot just presented is stunning.
Diggers struggles to recover from the defeat and tries to justify himself.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: Sergeant, please don't believe the nonsense he just said!

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: London needs imaginative art parties. It needs street fairs for everyone to get their voice heard.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: London is utopian.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: I will throw a feast for more people to have fun. By then, our philosophy will hit the headlines of all newspapers and become a new tidal trend. Everyone will get to know and fall in love!

items.speaker: Sergeant
items.text: Really?

items.speaker: Sergeant
items.text: But we only received countless complaints, about you particularly!

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: People just need some time to digest …

items.speaker: Iverson
items.text: London has been in chaos for too long. We need to thoroughly and completely root out all dangers and threats.

items.speaker: Sergeant
items.text: I am in total agreement, Mr. Iverson.

items.speaker: Sergeant
items.text: I think New Scotland Yard will further consider the importance of security robots in London.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: Disapprove! This is a violation of civil rights and a defiance to liberty!
A sudden ring interrupts Diggers's great speech.
Iverson snatches up the telephone from the robot's shoulder, like tearing up an arm from a doll's body.

items.speaker: Security Guard
items.text: Mr. ... Mr. Iverson, bad news ...

items.speaker: Security Guard
items.text: The Heart of London is gone …

items.speaker: Iverson
items.text: What?!
The passionate speaker has noticed that it's a perfect chance to escape other than wasting time talking.
TO BE CONTINUED ...
